text: If the member will yield, when you speak about {issue}, whose view are we hearing?
author: Codex writer B

text: When people back home ask about {issue}, whose view should I tell them you brought to the meeting?
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd like the sponsor to look at a change to {bill-name}. Should I bring it to you?
author: Codex writer B

text: My own. That's how I see {issue}, and I'm willing to vote that way.
author: Codex writer B

text: Put my name to it. Another member could look at {issue} and come down differently.
author: Codex writer B

text: I was speaking for the people I represent. Their stake in {issue} weighs most with me.
author: Codex writer B

text: The people back home. I tried to put their side of {issue} before the room.
author: Codex writer B

text: Yes. Bring me the section of {bill-name} you want to change. I'll read it with you.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd like to see your wording for {bill-name}. Could you mark the passage it would replace?
author: Codex writer B

text: Yes, you have the right person. I'd want to read the change alongside the rest of {bill-name} before taking a position.
author: Codex writer B

text: Whose position on {issue} should I take back to the neighborhood after this meeting?
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd like to get this straight before I repeat it. When you spoke about {issue}, who were you speaking for?
author: Codex writer B

text: May I ask the member whose judgment we just heard on {issue}?
author: Codex writer B

text: Suppose someone reads this debate and asks me who took that position on {issue}. Whom should I name?
author: Codex writer B

text: If somebody stops me on the way out and asks who spoke for that view on {issue}, what should I tell them?
author: Codex writer B

text: Can I check one thing about {issue} before we move on? Whose side were you putting to us just now?
author: Codex writer B

text: Mine. I put {bill-name} before this body. Any member joining me can speak for themselves.
author: Codex writer B

text: Back home you can say it came from the person who introduced {bill-name}. If somebody has a question about the wording, send them my way.
author: Codex writer B

text: Tell your neighbors I brought {bill-name} here. They can ask me why I wrote it that way.
author: Codex writer B

text: For myself. Sponsoring {bill-name} lets me explain what I meant when I wrote it. It doesn't let me answer for everybody here.
author: Codex writer B

text: That judgment was mine when I introduced {bill-name}, and it's mine today.
author: Codex writer B

text: Name me. Anyone reading the debate should be able to tell what the sponsor of {bill-name} had in mind.
author: Codex writer B

text: You can point me out. I'd be happy to stay and talk about why I brought {bill-name} in.
author: Codex writer B

text: My side, as the one who wrote {bill-name}. You'll have to ask the others where they stand.
author: Codex writer B

text: Mine. I think we ought to pass {bill-name}, and I'm willing to say why.
author: Codex writer B

text: I can answer for myself. I came to the floor to speak for {bill-name}.
author: Codex writer B

text: You're hearing my objection to {bill-name}. Other members can give you their own reasons.
author: Codex writer B

text: Mine. If you're asking who wants the chamber to turn down {bill-name}, count me.
author: Codex writer B

text: Tell them I favor {bill-name}. They can come to me if they'd like to talk it over.
author: Codex writer B

text: Give them my name. Moving ahead with {bill-name} makes sense to me.
author: Codex writer B

text: That's my reservation about {bill-name}. People back home have every right to see it differently.
author: Codex writer B

text: Say I asked the board to turn down {bill-name}. That's my own judgment.
author: Codex writer B

text: Take mine back. I'd be glad to explain to anybody on your block why I support {bill-name}.
author: Codex writer B

text: Tell the neighbors where I stand. I want {bill-name} to pass.
author: Codex writer B

text: You can say I spoke against {bill-name}. I wouldn't want the neighborhood to think you made that argument.
author: Codex writer B

text: My position. Anybody who wants to ask why I object to {bill-name} can ask me directly.
author: Codex writer B

text: For myself. If you repeat it, say I spoke in favor of {bill-name}.
author: Codex writer B

text: You heard my reading of {bill-name}. I think we ought to go ahead with it.
author: Codex writer B

text: Just me. I don't think {bill-name} ought to pass in its present form.
author: Codex writer B

text: I'd put it this way when you repeat it. I spoke against {bill-name}, and those reasons are mine.
author: Codex writer B

text: My judgment is that the chamber should pass {bill-name}. I'll leave the other members to give theirs.
author: Codex writer B

text: I reached that conclusion myself. It's the reason I rose in support of {bill-name}.
author: Codex writer B

text: My own judgment, and it's why I'm asking the chamber to reject {bill-name}.
author: Codex writer B

text: I have an objection to {bill-name}. I leave it to the other members to say whether they share it.
author: Codex writer B

text: Use my name. I want somebody reading this later to know who stood up for {bill-name}.
author: Codex writer B

text: You can attribute the argument for {bill-name} to me.
author: Codex writer B

text: Put me down as the one who spoke against {bill-name}. That's what I want the record to show.
author: Codex writer B

text: Name me. I'll stand by what I said about turning down {bill-name}.
author: Codex writer B

text: Send them over to me. I'd rather they heard straight from me why I want {bill-name} to pass.
author: Codex writer B

text: You can tell them I was for {bill-name}. That's the view I came to give.
author: Codex writer B

text: Point them my way. I can explain what troubles me about {bill-name}.
author: Codex writer B

text: Say it was me. If they want to know why I spoke against {bill-name}, I'll stay and talk.
author: Codex writer B

text: My side. I want us to go ahead with {bill-name}.
author: Codex writer B

text: I was giving my own reasons for backing {bill-name}. Anybody else on the board can come at it differently.
author: Codex writer B

text: That was my case against {bill-name}. Let the others on the board speak for themselves.
author: Codex writer B

text: Just my own. I think we'd be making a mistake by passing {bill-name}.
author: Codex writer B
